title: Multiplication formula for Hernandez and Leclerc's quivers with potentials

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction (list of multiplication-formula references) and Remark 4.6; References section
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites [Pal12], [XX09] in the introduction and [LM21] both in the introduction ("akin to [LM21, Conjecture 5.1]") and in Remark 4.6 ("This theorem gives an answer to the [LM21, Conjecture 5.1]"), but none of these three references appears in the bibliography. The [LM21] reference is especially important, since one of the paper's advertised contributions is answering a conjecture from it, yet the source cannot be identified.

It is claimed that "M[a,b] is equal to the image of q^{p_a} K^{(i_a)}_{(p_a-p_b)/2}" and that there is a sequence 0 → Φ^{-1}(M[a,b]) → q^{p_a} I_{i_a} --ε^{(p_a-p_b)/2}--> q^{p_b} I_{i_a} → 0. For an i-box [a,b] one has a ≤ b and the admissibility condition p_{s^+}=p_s+2 forces p_a ≤ p_b, so (p_a-p_b)/2 ≤ 0, while K^{(i)}_k is defined only for k ∈ Z_{>0} (eq. (4.4)-(4.5)). The index (and hence the power of ε) has the wrong sign.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Lemma 3.1 (last two displayed lines)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof concludes "z_1 - z_2 ∈ Hom_A(M_2, M_{1|W/W'})" and "q_η^{-1}(T',W') ≅ Hom_A(M_2, M_{1|W/W'})". The arguments are reversed: by construction z ∈ Hom_I(T', W/W') with T' a submodule of M_1 and W/W' a quotient of M_2, so the correct statement is z_1-z_2 ∈ Hom_A(M_1|_{T'}, M_2|_{W/W'}). As written the Hom space is between the wrong modules.

The argument "since T appears in the right hand of the above equation, we have Y = T for all Y in the right hand of the above equation, which implies that F_T = 2F_T" is a non sequitur: nothing excludes other strata Y ≠ T appearing in the sum, and even granting Y=T the displayed identity χ(PExt^1)F_T = (χ(PE(M_1,M_2)_T)+χ(PE(M_2,M_1)_T))F_T only yields F_T = 2F_T after dividing by the (unjustifiedly nonzero) Euler characteristic. Moreover the earlier step "It implies that there exists a short exact sequence 0→M_1→T→M_2→0 or 0→M_2→T→M_1→0" is asserted from g_T = g_{M_1}+g_{M_2} with no justification and is not used.

Three inconsistencies: (i) M[a,0] is used for arbitrary a ∈ Z_{<0}, but Definition 2.2 only defines M[a,b] for an i-box, which requires i_a = i_b, so [a,0] is generally not an i-box; (ii) the sum is taken over a ∈ Z_{<0}, omitting a = 0, whereas the relevant index set (initial seed, Q^-_{GLS}) is Z_{≤0}; (iii) the Gabriel quiver of End_A(M^{-∞}) is claimed to equal Q_{GLS} (indexed by all of Z), while a module indexed by negative integers can at best give Q^-_{GLS} ≅ Γ^-.

Theorem 2.3 asserts that "M^{-∞} ... is a rigid module", while its proof begins "Following the above Lemma and [KKOP24, Theorem 7.20], M^{-∞} is a tilting module over A". Rigidity and tiltingness are different statements, and the introduction speaks of a "tilting object"; the paper never reconciles these.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 (standing assumption) vs. Eq. (4.2), Section 2.2, and the definition of ε
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states "For the purposes of this paper, we assume C to be simply-laced, implying its symmetry, where C = B" (so d_i = 1, lacing number r = 1, b_ii = 2), yet subsequent material is written for general symmetrizable C: Eq. (4.2) contains factors for c_{ji} = -2 and c_{ji} = -3, the relations in §2.2 use exponents -c_{ij} > 1, ε = Σ ε_i^{r/d} e_i invokes the lacing number, and d_i appears throughout. The standing assumption contradicts the generality in which the results are stated.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 3.2 (statement) and Eq. (3.13) in its proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 3.2 is stated for arbitrary modules M_1, M_2 over A, but its proof relies on the perpendicularity relation (3.13) E(M_1,M_2)^⊥_{T',W'} = E(M_2,M_1)_{W',T'}, i.e. on the nondegenerate duality Ext^1_A(M_1,M_2) ≅ D Ext^1_A(M_2,M_1). That duality is established in Proposition 2.1 only under the hypothesis that the modules are locally free over Π(l) for some l; the hypothesis is silently dropped.

The text refers to "formula (3.6)", but no equation (3.6) exists in the paper: numbering jumps from (3.5) to (3.7). A key step of the construction of q_η therefore refers to a nonexistent displayed formula.

The right-hand side is written as F_{K^{(i)}_{i,r}}; the module in question is K^{(i)}_{k,r} (the kernel defined for the integer k appearing on the left-hand side). The subscript 'i' makes the formula ill-defined and inconsistent with the definition of K^{(i)}_{k,m} given later in Section 4.

Section 4 defines K^{(i)}_{k,m} as "the kernel of a generic A-module homomorphism from I_{i,m} to I_{i, m-k b_{ii}}" (target index decreasing), whereas Definition 2.2 and the proof of Lemma 4.4 define the same type of module as the kernel of I_{(i_a,p_a)} → I_{(i_b,p_b)} with p_b > p_a (target index increasing). The two conventions are incompatible.

The diagram is supposed to display the oriented cycle through (i,m), (j,m+b_{ij}), (i,m+2b_{ij}), ..., (i,m+2b_{ij}+b_{ii}) = (i,m). As printed it contains a vertex (i, m-b_{ii}) with arrows to both (i,m) and (j,m+b_{ij}), which is not an arrow of Γ as defined by the rule ((i,r)→(j,s)) ⟺ s = r+b_{ij}, and it simultaneously lists (i,m) and (i,m+2b_{ij}+b_{ii}), which coincide; the depicted graph is not the closed oriented cycle described in the text.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 4.5 ("The dominant monomial of L_1 ⊗ L_2 is unique")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claim that the dominant monomial of L_1 ⊗ L_2 is unique is false in general: by the very set-up of the theorem the product decomposes as z^{g'}F_T + P with P ≠ 0 containing other simple constituents, each contributing its own dominant monomial. What is true is only that the highest (maximal) dominant monomial m_1m_2 occurs with multiplicity one; the proof's conclusion g' = g_1+g_2 is thus based on a false statement as written.

"Since T is a rigid module, it follows that T = M_1 * M_2 or T = M_2 * M_1" is asserted without proof; the existence of a short exact sequence 0→M_1→T→M_2→0 with T rigid does not by itself identify T with the generic extension, yet this is the paper's main stated conclusion (the link to [LM21, Conjecture 5.1]). Additionally the sequences are written with undefined symbols M_{L_1}, M_{L_2}, I_1, I_2, and the injective copresentation 0 → M_i → I_1^{g_i^-} → I_2^{g_i^+} → 0 has the ± superscripts interchanged relative to the convention used in the proof of Lemma 4.4 (where g = +1 at the sub-injective).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 / Section 4 (document structure around Lemma 4.4, Theorem 4.5 and the proof of Theorem 2.3)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proofs are scrambled: Lemma 4.4 is stated with no proof following it; Theorem 4.5's proof begins, is cut off after "g' = g_1 + g_2", and is then interrupted by what is clearly the proof of Lemma 4.4 (about determinantal modules M[a,b]) and by the proof of Theorem 2.3, after which Theorem 4.5's proof resumes without any indication. As printed, which argument proves which statement cannot be determined.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.2 (definition of Π / Π̃ and of ε)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The algebra is defined as "the k-algebra Π" (quotient of kQ̃), but from (2.4) onwards everything is written for Π̃ (Π̃-gmod, Π(l) = Π̃/ε^l Π̃, Ext^1_{Π̃}), which is never defined. Moreover ε = Σ_i ε_i^{r/d} e_i uses an undefined symbol d (presumably d_i) and reuses r, which elsewhere denotes a vertex coordinate.

The duality Ext^1(M,N) ≅ D Ext^1(N,M) in GLS17 is proved for locally free modules over their generalized preprojective algebra Π, which includes the nilpotency relations ε_i^{c_i}=0, whereas the algebra used here (defined by relations (1) and (2) only, with ε_i not nilpotent) is a different, infinite-dimensional algebra. Applying the cited theorem verbatim to Π̃-modules is not justified in the text.

predicted_errors.error_location: Opening sentence of Section 2.3 vs. Theorem 2.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 2.3 announces "we aim to realize the algebra A as the endomorphism ring of a tilting module over the preprojective algebra of Q", but the result actually proved (Theorem 2.3) goes the other way: it exhibits a (tilting/rigid) module M^{-∞} over A and computes the Gabriel quiver of End_A(M^{-∞}); A is never realized as an endomorphism ring over the preprojective algebra of Q.

The entry gives "Selecta Mathematica, 14(3):59–119, 2008" for Derksen–Weyman–Zelevinsky, Quivers with potentials and their representations I; the paper appeared in Selecta Math. (N.S.) 14 (2008), no. 1, pp. 59–119. The issue number is wrong.
